title: Area-resolved GLMM on the omission-relative baseline: the three subjects disagree in SIGN, so the corpus-wide low-frequency effect is null at the session level

goal.text: omission-a's LFP claims are stated at the unit of inference the design supports, with the direction and magnitude of every band effect derived from a fitted model rather than asserted.
goal.falsifier: Closed when every LFP sentence in the manuscript is traceable to a row of outputs/lfp_band_census_v2/glmm_summary.csv, and no sentence generalises across subjects a band effect whose sign reverses between them.

notes: STEP 3c/3d of the four-step plan. Census: scripts/compute_channel_band_power_census_v2.py (711/711 omission files, 0 skipped, 293,760 rows, 17 sessions, 3 subjects, 12 areas, median 39 trials per channel, 2,690 s). Models: scripts/fit_omission_band_power_glmm.py.

RESPONSE: db_mid_omirel = 10*log10(power in the omitted slot / power in the -250 to -50 ms omission-relative baseline), trial-averaged within channel. The baseline sits inside the delay immediately preceding the omitted slot -- itself one of the three visually identical empty periods -- so this is the middle o against the late part of the first o, not against a neutral pre-trial state. A pre-trial fixation-relative measure (db_mid_fxrel) is emitted alongside it and is uniformly more negative, because it also absorbs up to 3.6 s of within-trial drift.

CHANNEL-LEVEL VS SESSION-LEVEL. Channel-level fits give |z| above 40 on sub-decibel effects, because neighbouring contacts on one shank see overlapping field potentials and are treated as independent. Every model therefore has a session-level companion that collapses to one observation per session before fitting. The session-level numbers are the ones the design supports; the channel-level ones are retained only to show how far the naive standard errors are off.

HEADLINE 1 -- THE CORPUS-WIDE LOW-FREQUENCY EFFECT DOES NOT SURVIVE. Session level, n = 17 sessions: theta -0.53 dB (p = 0.066), alpha -0.37 (p = 0.18), beta -0.22 (p = 0.28), low gamma -0.06 (p = 0.55), high gamma +0.13 (p = 0.069). Nothing significant, and every low-frequency point estimate is NEGATIVE. The channel-level version reaches q = 0.005 for theta purely on inflated degrees of freedom.

HEADLINE 2 -- THE SUBJECTS DISAGREE IN SIGN, WHICH IS WHY THE POOLED TEST IS NULL. Session-level, per subject, BH across bands. C31o (8 sessions): theta -1.58 dB q = 5.0e-5, alpha -1.36 q = 1.0e-4, beta -0.89 q = 0.0043, low gamma -0.39 q = 0.0020 -- decreases, all significant. V182o (4 sessions): theta +0.56 p = 0.049, low gamma +0.28 q = 0.0012, high gamma +0.27 q = 0.0019 -- increases. V198o (5 sessions): nothing significant; alpha +0.71 and beta +0.62 trend positive. Two animals go one way and one goes the other, so pooling cancels.

HEADLINE 3 -- THE V3 EXCEPTION SURVIVES IN DIRECTION AND MAGNITUDE BUT NOT IN SIGNIFICANCE. The only subject-controlled test is model D: within V198o, the V3a/d probe against the V1/V2 probe of the SAME five sessions. Paired across sessions: beta +1.59 dB (p = 0.076), alpha +1.16 (p = 0.24), low gamma +0.56 (p = 0.24), high gamma -0.17 (p = 0.60), theta +0.07 (p = 0.81). The effect is large for a band-power contrast and the sign is the predicted one, but n = 5 sessions and it does not reach significance. The channel-level version of the same contrast gives beta z = 70, which is an artefact of treating 11,520 channel observations as independent.

THE CONFOUND IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL. Cross-tabulating area against subject: V3 is recorded only in C31o; V3a and V3d only in V198o; FEF, FST, MST, MT, PFC and TEO only in C31o and V182o; V1 and V2 in C31o and V198o. No area is recorded in all three animals. A between-area coefficient in the corpus therefore cannot be separated from a between-animal difference, which is why model C is emitted as descriptive and model D exists at all.

MODEL C, SESSION LEVEL, DESCRIPTIVE. Relative to V1: V3a/d beta +1.82 dB (q = 1.6e-6), alpha +1.32 (q = 0.0058), low gamma +0.52 (q = 0.0042); PFC alpha +1.02 (q = 0.027) and low gamma +0.44 (q = 0.011); FEF low gamma +0.44 (q = 0.021). These are the numbers that would headline an area-resolved figure, and every one of them is confounded with subject.

CORRECTION APPENDED 2026-07-28 (Hamm). The framing of HEADLINE 1 was wrong and is superseded. Model A tests whether the SIGNED mean, pooled across areas that move in opposite directions, differs from zero -- a test of common DIRECTION, not of whether modulation exists. Reported as 'the corpus-wide low-frequency effect does not survive' it misdescribes the data. Against each channel's own baseline the mean ABSOLUTE change is 1.18 dB in alpha, 1.16 dB in theta, 0.91 dB in beta, against 0.59 dB in low gamma and 0.42 dB in high gamma: low-frequency modulation is roughly twice gamma modulation and is present at every site. The correct statement is large modulation with no shared sign. The p-values in HEADLINE 1 are arithmetically right and remain the answer to the direction question; the sentence built on them was not.

SECOND CORRECTION, SAME TURN. The analysis window understates every effect above. The response does not resolve within the omitted slot: area traces show low-frequency power still climbing at +1000 ms. The 0 to +531 ms window therefore samples the leading edge of a ramp. This applies to the model D V3 contrast (+1.59 dB beta) as much as to the pooled estimates. Superseded by the time-resolved extraction (scripts/extract_omission_tfr_maps.py), which stores the full frequency axis over -1000 to +1000 ms and reports the omitted-slot, post-omission-delay and union windows separately.

LAMINAR MODEL SKIPPED, NOT NULL. vFLIP2 returns 'na' for roughly two thirds of channels in the sessions processed so far, so layer coverage is far below the 50 percent floor the script requires. A laminar claim fitted on the channels where the crossover happened to converge would be selection, not anatomy. Recorded as a skip with its reason rather than as an absence of laminar structure.
issues: omission-a's stated thesis has two LFP legs. 'Widespread low-frequency modulation across the hierarchy' is CONTRADICTED as written: the pooled session-level effect is null, and where it is significant within an animal the sign is a decrease, not an elevation. The V3 exception is SUPPORTED in direction and magnitude but is underpowered (p = 0.076 on 5 sessions) and rests on a single animal.

The prior draft's assertion of sustained beta ELEVATION during omission is not reproduced at any level of analysis: channel-level, session-level, pooled and within-subject all give a decrease in C31o, a null in V198o, and a small increase only in V182o.
Model D could be fitted in only one of three subjects; C31o and V182o have no session in which V3 and V1/V2 sit on separate probes.

The descriptive Clopper-Pearson proportions (fraction of channels with |db| >= 1) treat channels as independent and understate uncertainty; they are marked descriptive in the receipt and must not be reported as inferential.
V3a/d elevation cannot be distinguished from a V198o animal effect by any test available in this corpus.
plan: Rewrite the omission-a Results LFP subsection around the subject-level disagreement rather than a corpus-wide claim; a headline that states a negative result is house style (two of four headings in the exemplar do).
State the V3 result as a within-subject, within-session probe contrast of +1.59 dB in beta at p = 0.076, n = 5 sessions -- not as an established area difference.
Decide with Hamm whether omission-a's LFP leg is retitled around what the data support, or whether the paper's scope narrows to the spiking result with the LFP demoted to a figure.
Re-run scripts/build_channel_area_vector.py and the GLMM once vFLIP finishes all 21 sessions, to record final layer coverage; the laminar model is expected to remain skipped.

verification.receipt: outputs/lfp_band_census_v2/receipt.json (711 files processed, 0 skipped, 293,760 rows) and outputs/lfp_band_census_v2/glmm_results.json + glmm_summary.csv. Models fitted with statsmodels 0.14.6 MixedLM, REML, lbfgs; session-level companions by one-sample and paired t on session means. BH applied across the five bands within each (model, term, subject). All p-values quoted above are read from glmm_summary.csv, not recomputed by hand.

links.reasoning: Every area-resolved number here is computed on channels selected by that area vector, and inherits its equal-share assumption.
This is the first area-resolved band-power result in which no channel contributes to two areas.
Fills the LFP [[STAT]] slots and contradicts the draft's sustained-elevation direction; the Results LFP subsection must be rewritten before v2.
The response variable is the middle of the three visually identical empty periods against the late part of the first, exactly as the paradigm node specifies.
Removes disqualifiers 1 and 4 for the LFP results (numbers now computed from data, group labels no longer alias) while creating a substantive scope question the score cannot resolve.
